speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether the Tray and Crockery Return Rate under the mandatory tray return policy has been maintained at 90% and above since the last update in September 2022; and (b) whether there continues to be regular checks being conducted so as to ensure overall cleanliness is maintained in hawker centres, coffeeshops and food courts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The average TCRR of around 90% largely shows that many diners have been doing their part.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We hope that more diners will return their trays and used crockery after their meals, to entrench this as a social norm in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have one supplementary question for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In general, I have received feedback that some patrons, although they are able to, do not return their trays after eating.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And if so, would the Ministry be able to impose more effective measures, like more frequent patrolling by NEA officers and enforcement, only if necessary?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have mentioned in my reply earlier, the average TCRR for our hawker centres, coffee shops and food courts have remained at around 90%.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, we are heartened by the support given by Singaporeans to clear and clean up after themselves.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We do want to encourage more Singaporeans to clean up after themselves at our public dining places.
